title: Flowframe: continuous workload fingerprinting and safe apply for dynamic micro-windowing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build and ship 'Flowframe', a lightweight continuous workload fingerprinting service and safe-apply pipeline that generates per-route micro-windowing (micro-batching) and cache-preservation hints. These hints feed the runtime's dynamic coalescer to reduce per-token cost while preserving P99 latency and output fidelity. Flowframe must operate safely in production: provide shadow trials, progressive canaries, automated rollback triggers, and a human readable audit trail for every configuration change.

Why now: We see a large fraction of redundant KV-requests and short-sequence requests that can be coalesced with small windows without hurting latency for most routes. A conservative, automated approach will unlock meaningful cost savings for Hosted API customers and Dedicated pools while minimizing user-visible regressions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Flowframe synthesizes a fingerprint for every route with: token length distribution, sequential correlation score, KV-cache-hit-estimate, and cold-start frequency.
2) For a given route, Flowframe proposes a candidate micro-window (size, max_delay_ms, kv_preserve flag) and estimated cost delta and latency risk.
3) The runtime can ingest Flowframe hints via a secure config endpoint and apply shadow configuration (no traffic impact).
4) Shadow trials run for N=24h and collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rate, and semantic regression proxies (embedding drift).
5) Canary rollout path supports staged application 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic halt/rollback on any trigger.
6) Rollbacks occur automatically and create an incident-like entry with reason, metrics snapshot, and PR reference.
7) End-to-end tests and load tests demonstrate <=5% additional median latency and <3% chance of p99 increase >10% in canary scenarios.
8) Documentation: Confluence playbook, console UI hook to preview suggested hint, and one example customer-facing note template are published.
implementation_steps:
1) Telemetry adapter: implement lightweight streaming fingerprint extractor in runtime, emits compact fingerprints every 5m per route (proto-lite).
2) Store selector: create a tiered retention path for fingerprints (24h high-res, 30d summary).
3) Heuristic engine: implement rule-set that maps fingerprint features to candidate micro-windows using conservative defaults + tunable hysteresis.
4) Safety harness: shadow application path + diffing collector; store differential metrics.
5) Rollout controller: implement staged deployer that supports percent-based allocation and abort on pre-defined triggers.
6) Console integration: add UI to surface suggestion, preview expected cost delta, and trigger manual apply.
7) Infra: secure ingestion webhook and RBAC for programmatic applies.
8) Tests: unit ruleset tests, shadow-run integration tests, chaos tests that simulate KV-latency spikes.
9) Docs & runbook: publish Confluence playbook and add runbook to PagerDuty escalation policy.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (shadow only): 0% traffic (rolling for 24h) across 10 routes representing diverse workloads. Phase 1 (canary micro-apply): 1% traffic for 6h -> evaluate triggers. Phase 2: 5% for 12h -> evaluate. Phase 3: 25% for 24h -> evaluate. Phase 4: 100% apply for route. Safe-apply default schedule forces at least 24h of shadow observation and requires embedding-drift < 0.02 (cosine distance median) before progressing beyond 1% canary. All phases log audit entries and require at least two successful gate checks with different monitoring windows.

Abort conditions (immediate rollback): p99 latency increase > 10% absolute, error rate increase > 0.5 percentage points, spike in 5xxs > 50% of baseline, embedding-drift median > 0.05, manual abort by SRE/PM/owner.
metrics_and_triggers:
Primary metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), request error rate (%), 5xx count, tokens-per-request, KV-hit-estimate (%), cost-per-1000-tokens ($). Secondary metrics: embedding-drift-proxy (median cosine distance), output-length-shift, tail memory pressure.
Trigger thresholds (initial): p99_up_10pct -> immediate rollback; error_rate_up_0.5ppt -> pause rollout; kv_hit_drop_>15pct_in_10min -> pause and alert; cost_improvement_expected_<0.2pct -> flag for manual review (too small to risk). Triggers are configurable per-customer in Dedicated mode.
rollback_playbook:
On trigger: 1) Halt rollout immediately. 2) Execute automatic rollback to previous config. 3) Create audit entry with snapshot of last 3 hours of metrics and the candidate hint. 4) Run diagnostics job that replays a sample of shadow requests through both configs to produce diff heatmaps. 5) Notify owners and SRE via Slack and PagerDuty. 6) If rollback fails, escalate to on-call runtime kernel engineer. 7) Postmortem: required for any rollback that lasts >1h or affects >5% traffic.
Mitigation knobs: temporary rate-limit tightening, route-level fallback to smaller model variant, increase request timeout conservatively.
telemetry_requirements:
- Fingerprint message fields: route_id, time_window_start, token_length_histogram (buckets), seq_correlation_score, kv_hit_estimate, cold_start_count, sample_seed.
- Overhead budget: fingerprint transmitter must add <0.2% CPU and <2KB/request aggregated per-minute per-route.
- Retention: 24h high-res (5m buckets), 30d rollup.
- Privacy: strip PII prompts at source; do not store raw prompt text.
- Sampling: deterministic reservoir sample for semantic regression checks with seed tied to route id.
